title: Adic and rational smooth dualizing complexes
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, and let $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be a
separated finite-type smooth morphism of pure dimension $d$. The
dualizing complex

$$
\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda
$$

has the canonical identification

$$
\omega_{X,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d]
$$

obtained by inverting the integral purity map of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction]
when $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, and its transported purity map of
[thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] when $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$; the counit
identifies with the transported normalized integration map

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d)[2d])\longrightarrow\Lambda.
$$

proof.text: Use the finite normalized coefficient model of [def-pur-adic-finite-comparison-model]. Its declaration-preserving extraction includes the proved unique root comparison, the two existing finite projection and realization obligations, and the explicit finitePowerComparison construction. The finite unit is a degree-zero single complex: exact derived site inverse image preserves its lower bound zero, proving finiteUnitPlus. The structure morphism is over Spec k because Spec.map of the identity is identity. These constructions preserve the integral/rational/common-stage unit route below.

source.place: coefficient-unit application; elementary finite-model preliminaries in the Lean realization

proof.text: For integralTwist_mem, map the existing coefficient-prime unit in each local ring to its residue field and choose its uniquely determined inverse. The existing signed integral coefficient-twist membership theorem gives the unshifted nonnegative root power. Intrinsic integral constructibility is triangulated, hence stable under the even shift 2d. The integral residue-Tor criterion identifies this constructibility predicate with integral finite-Tor constructibility, completing the membership proof for every scheme over the fixed base, without finite-type restrictions.

source.place: Completed coefficient unit and shifted Tate line in the coefficient-unit application.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $U=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$. By [lem-pur-completed-unit-pullback-tower], $U\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\mathcal O_E)$, its reductions are the coefficient units with common Tor interval $[0,0]$, and $La_X^*U\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$. Apply [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] using the compatible family of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]. Its hypotheses hold: $X,s$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $a_X$ is smooth separated of pure dimension $d\ge0$. It gives $\gamma_{a_X,U}:\mathcal O_{E,X}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,\mathcal O_E}$, with the specified finite reductions. Invert it; $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ denotes the completed unit.

The rational and common-stage units are presented by $U$, and their pullbacks are $E_X$ and $(\Qlb)_X$, by [lem-pur-completed-unit-pullback-tower]. Apply [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] to $a_X$ at these units. Step 1 checks its geometric hypotheses and supplies its normalized integral lattice. The resulting isomorphisms are exactly the coefficient transports of integral purity; invert them to obtain $\omega_{X,\Lambda}\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ for $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$.

Write $\eta_\Lambda=\gamma_{a_X,\Lambda_s}^{-1}$. Reading the counit through $\eta_\Lambda$ gives $\epsilon_\Lambda\circ Ra_{X!}(\gamma_{a_X,\Lambda_s})$. At finite level this is the smooth trace by [def-pur-smooth-trace]. The integral and field-stage composites are its specified transports by [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence] and [prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence]. Apply [lem-pur-point-trace-reconstruction] to these coherent counit pairings: their point-fibre values have source $R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d)[2d])$ and target $\Lambda$, with the same normalization under coefficient transport. The affine-space clause of [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] supplies that normalization: for $p_d:\mathbf A_k^d\to s$ (both schemes separated finite type), the finite trace is the ordered product of normalized affine-line traces and sends their $d$-fold class to $1$. Its coefficient-transport clause preserves this normalization, including $d=0$. No class integrating to $1$ is asserted for arbitrary $X$. The Lean counit assembly is complete: the integral normalization is the specification of the uniquely chosen integral identification. A proved categorical helper cancels q and b and uses naturality of q to transport a counit read through an isomorphism. Apply it first to rationalization, then to the selected small-model scalar extension, then to common-stage inclusion. At each later stage the previous counit equation, precomposed with the compact-support image of the inverse identification, recovers exactly the previously defined integration map. These are precisely rationalIdentification, rationalIntegration, closedIdentification and closedIntegration.

proof_origin.note: The integral/rational/common-stage unit route is retained. Proved existsUnique_rootComparison from finite Tate descent and local-root-tensor extensionality. Proved the final counit assembly from the integral identification specification and the three coefficient-comparison counit laws. Proved integralTwist_mem from signed-line membership, shift stability and the integral residue-Tor criterion. Four original holes remain, no new holes. Existing finite-power and finite-comparison blocks are extracted for compile time; two new fully constructed helper definitions cache original comparison endpoints.

blueprint_update.statement:
Work in the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions], let
$\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ with the condensed categories
$\Dbc(-,\Lambda)$ of [def-sf-setting], and let $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be a
separated finite-type smooth morphism of pure dimension $d$. The
dualizing complex

$$
\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda
$$

has the canonical identification

$$
\omega_{X,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d]
$$

obtained from [sk-thm-purity-transport]. Through it, the counit becomes the
smooth trace

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d)[2d])\longrightarrow\Lambda
$$

of [sk-def-sp-trace]. Its reductions modulo $\pi_E^n$ (for
$\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$) are the finite normalized integration maps of
[cor-pur-finite-stage-smooth-dualizing-complex]. For $\Lambda=E$ it is the
integral one with $\ell$ inverted, and for $\Lambda=\Qlb$ the extension of
scalars of the one over a finite $E$.

proof.text:
Apply [sk-thm-purity-transport] to $f=a_X$ and $K=\Lambda_{\Spec k}$. Since
$a_X^*\Lambda_{\Spec k}=\Lambda_X$, the purity isomorphism
$\gamma_{a_X,\Lambda}(\Lambda_{\Spec k})$ identifies $\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ with
$\omega_{X,\Lambda}$. By definition of the smooth trace ([sk-def-sp-trace]), the
counit $\varepsilon_{a_X}(\Lambda)$ composed with $Ra_{X!}$ of this identification
is $\operatorname{Tr}_{a_X}(\Lambda_{\Spec k})$. Its description through the
finite traces is the final assertion of [det-sp-purity-coefficient-change],
whose items (1)–(3) treat reduction, inversion of $\ell$ and extension of
scalars, applied to the finite traces of
[cor-pur-finite-stage-smooth-dualizing-complex].
